answer_1.quote: We present We-bCiteS, a Chinese dataset for Attributed Query-Focused Summarization (AQFS). As shown in Figure , given a query and the retrieved documents, AQFS aims to summarize all pertinent information from the documents with in-line citations to make the summary attributable.
answer_1.outputs: summarize all pertinent information from the documents with in-line citations

answer_2.quote: We adopt the following metrics to evaluate the utility of the summaries: Length. We report the average summary length... Self-BLEU... Claim precision... Claim recall... Claim F1... AIS... ACS... Citation precision... Citation recall... Citation F1.

answer_3.quote: We first prompt ChatGPT to extract the sub-claims in sentences since have validated this approach via human assessment.

answer_4.quote: We collaborated with crowdsourcing companies for data labeling. We recruited a team of 27 annotators, 7 quality inspectors, and 1 senior quality inspector, all underwent a monthlong training.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators would cite all supporting documents for verification-worthy sentences, correct groundedness and coherence errors, and supplement missing information.
